gap: No result ChatGPT got states a timed print by a named reviewer for the candidates: AndroidPCTV timed a PLA 3DBenchy on the QIDI Max4 at 18 min (2026-02-27) and The Technology Man timed one on the Bambu Lab X2D at 24 min (2026-06-10), and The Technology Man measured an average 330 W across an overnight ABS print on the X2D.
standout_why: All three cited desktop3dprinters.us lists (fastest-3d-printers, high-speed-printer-specs; enclosed-corexy-printers is the same claimed-spec format) say outright that every speed, acceleration and flow figure is the maker's claim, not a measured print time. 3dprintgearlab's CoreXY page (cited in chat 2) carries one measured figure, Tom's Hardware's 160 mm/s average for the Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2, and nothing measured for the X2D, H2S, Max4, Plus5, Q2 or K2 Plus. ChatGPT itself said it found no controlled ABS benchmark. The only measured ABS time among the results is on QIDI's own blog (rank 6, not cited): Aurora Tech's 3 h 13 min ABS pencil case on the older Plus 4, which the page says does not carry over to the Plus5.
decides: It does not settle 'fastest at ABS'. No named reviewer published a same-model ABS print time for the X2D, H2S, Max4, Plus5 or K2 Plus that could be opened. The measured Benchy times are PLA runs with different profiles and testers, so they show the claimed-speed ranking is not the measured one: the 800 mm/s Max4's 18 min Benchy beat the 1,000 mm/s X2D's 24 min. That supports ChatGPT's own caveat and lets the page say plainly that the claimed top speed is not a measured ABS result. It gives a modest point for the QIDI Max4, which Dealectric lists, over ranking by claimed speed alone. The X2D's 330 W ABS figure gives an ABS running cost, not a speed.
